from.place: Since the finite ring $\Lambda=P_n$ is annihilated by an integer, $F_{\Et}$ is a torsion abelian sheaf, so the classical input of the source note (Th. 1.1 of SGA 4 1/2 and [Tag 095U](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095U)) applies to $f_{\Et}$: the sheaves $R^qf_{\Et,*}F_{\Et}$ are constructible and zero for $q>2e$.

title: Constructibility of etale compact-support candidates over a qcqs base
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $p$ proper and $f=pj$, and write $Rf_!^{(j,p)}K=Rp_*j_!K$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], where $j_!$ is applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $Rp_*$ is the derived direct image for $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] have constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal H^q(Rf_!^{(j,p)}K)$ is a constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GL0, label theorem-constructible-shriek, bounded-below finite-ring specialization; section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification (compact-support candidate)

proof.text: For a fixed candidate R=Rp_*j_!, exactness of j_! and left t-exactness of right derived direct image show that R preserves every lower cohomological bound. Suppose R sends constructible sheaves in degree zero to complexes with constructible cohomology. For a bounded-below constructible complex K and degree n, truncate above n. This truncation is bounded constructible. Induction on its amplitude using truncation triangles and the constructible weak Serre class shows that its R-image has constructible cohomology. In the image of the truncation triangle, the third term is concentrated in degrees at least n+1. The long exact sequence therefore identifies H^n(R tau_{<=n}K) with H^n(RK). This proves the bounded-below assertion from the sheaf assertion. In Lean the bounded-amplitude induction is the already proved source lemma prop_of_boundedConstructible in ConstructibleDirectImage; the remaining truncation comparison is written explicitly.

Over an affine base Y, induct on n to prove constructibility for the projection A^n_Y -> Y on bounded-below constructible inputs. For n=0 the projection is an isomorphism, so use the closed-immersion consequence of quasi-finite constructibility. For n+1 reindex the coordinates as n coordinates and one coordinate, giving A^(n+1)_Y isomorphic over Y to A^1_(A^n_Y). The isomorphism preserves constructibility by the same closed-immersion theorem. Apply the affine-line sheaf theorem and step 1 to its projection, then the induction hypothesis to A^n_Y -> Y. Compact-support composition identifies the result for the given compactification. The compactifications of affine-space projections are the explicit projective-space constructions of the source library, via HasCompactification.affineSpace_over; the compactification after the isomorphism is obtained by precomposition. General Nagata compactification is unnecessary.

For an affine source X over an affine base Y, finite presentation gives finitely many generators for its coordinate algebra. Enumerate them by ULift(Fin n). The associated map i:X -> A^n_Y is a closed immersion: its map on global sections is surjective because its image contains both the base-ring image and every chosen generator. The factorization i followed by the affine-space projection equals f. The closed immersion i is locally of finite presentation, by cancellation for a locally finitely presented composite through a finite-type morphism (the proved source lemma locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp). Use the proper compactification of i and the explicit compactification of the projection. Quasi-finite constructibility handles i, step 2 handles the projection, and compact-support composition proves the affine case for the original compactification.

For qcqs X over affine Y, choose a finite affine cover, including the empty affine open to handle empty X uniformly. Induct on the number of cover members. A one-member cover makes X affine. Otherwise write X=V union W, with W affine and V covered by one fewer members. These opens and their intersection are quasi-compact, and their scheme structures are quasi-separated. Their morphisms to Y retain separation and finite presentation. The intersection V cap W has a cover by one fewer affine opens, because separation over the affine base makes the intersections of affine opens affine. Exact inverse image commutes with cohomology and preserves constructibility, so the induction applies to V and V cap W, while step 3 applies to W. Precompose the given compactification to obtain all three open compactifications. The relative Mayer--Vietoris triangle then gives the result on X: the first two terms have constructible cohomology, finite biproducts preserve constructibility, and the weak Serre class is closed under the long exact cohomology sequence.

For arbitrary qcqs Y, restrict to each affine open W. The pullback X_W is qcqs, the pullback morphism remains separated of finite presentation, and the pulled-back complex has constructible cohomology by exact inverse image and constructible pullback. Apply step 4. Finite-coefficient compact-support base change identifies the output with the restriction of the original output. Exact inverse image identifies their homology sheaves. The qcqs affine-local criterion now proves constructibility of the original output in every degree. The comparison between finite-value and finite-stalk definitions of constructible module sheaves is the proved source equivalence isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf.

Transport the result from the bounded-below candidate to the fixed total candidate along rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusCompatibility, then apply the homology functor. This natural isomorphism is part of the already proved implementation of the candidate; it changes neither the compactification nor the original input complex. Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GL0, affine-space induction, finite source cover, and affine-local base reduction; bounded-below passage uses truncation devissage instead of the spectral sequence; Lean proof by M3, 2026-10-18

The delivery adds no new nodes, the statement and Lean record are unchanged, every step is under 2000 characters, the dependency closure has no cycle, and no SGA source is cited. Step 6 (new): f_T is locally of finite presentation by the 01TQ node, using affine opens inside T. Its diagonal is the base change of Delta_f along the open T x_Y T, so it is closed (proper-fp-permanence (b)). f_T is quasi-compact by 03GI (T quasi-compact, Y quasi-separated). qcqs-over-affine then makes T qcqs, so f_T has finite presentation. No step assumes what it proves. Step 7 (new, marked elementary): restriction is exact (prop node (3)), the exact-functor node (c) carries cohomology, and 095E (3)=>(1) on X followed by (1)=>(3) on T gives constructibility. It really is elementary. Step 8 (new): the induction on the number of affine opens is set up correctly. The 01KP node gives U cap V a cover by m-1 affine opens, so both induction calls strictly decrease m. The Mayer-Vietoris node (0GKN) applies with quasi-compact U and V and any chosen compactifications. The long exact sequence and the Serre node give kernel, cokernel and extension closure. Step 9: thm-cbc-finite-torsion places no condition on the open W -> Y and works with finite Lambda in D^+. Coefficient category and exchange map match Rp_*j_!. Edge cases checked: empty X, n=0, Lambda=0, coefficients of residue characteristic with nothing inverted, K bounded below only. The tool uses are acceptable.
